rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this round increases obfuscation pressure. Fhourstones is a search-heavy benchmark whose hot path is the alpha-beta routine 'ab' (2085 of 4861 text bytes), so runtime-heavy transforms get elevated SecurityGain but restrained RuntimeCost weights: FLA is the strongest structural defender and is pushed hardest (0.8/0.7), while its RuntimeCost weight of 0.45 keeps it from saturating the hot recursive search; BCF is deliberately lower (0.7) with low RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.35/0.3) because bogus-control-flow multiplies both text size and execution cost with less per-byte security than flattening. SUB is cheap and correctness-safe, so it gets a broad high weight to blanket all 23 functions including small helpers where bigger passes fit poorly. IBR and ICALL are favored (0.8/0.75) since indirect control flow substantially raises static analysis difficulty at moderate cost, and IGV adds global-variable indirection that hides the game-board state accesses central to this program. SPLIT rounds out coverage with modest weights, and all CorrectnessRisk weights stay low since round 1 showed the pipeline is stable and correctness must be preserved.
